data.name: describe_phenotype
data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density higher vs DMSO; 12 observations; candidates: Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown

observations.finding: DMSO (f_a8be9aee1b01): dense fields, 100s cells, clustered epithelial sheets and spindle single cells. Blue nuclei oval uniform size. Green tubulin diffuse filamentous network filling cytoplasm. Red actin as peripheral cortex and stress fibers.
w_da9f3d3374 0.3uM (f_1b65e7d82403, f_eb575406d3ac): cell density modestly reduced vs DMSO but still ~30-40 cells/field = 72 cells measured. Consistent with DMSO morphology not catastrophic loss.

w_da9f3d3374 0.3uM: cell shape markedly irregular/stellate with thin spiky projections and dendritic extensions in red/green overlay. Outline less solid, less round/compact vs DMSO rounded-polygonal cells. e.g. star-shaped cells bottom left f_1b65e7d82403, elongated bipolar cells center.

Measurement cell_roundness z=-12.25 (0.485 vs 0.562), cell_solidity z=-8.69 (0.795 vs 0.85), cell_eccentricity z=-5.19 (0.736 vs 0.771) support less round, less solid, less elliptical - irregular stellate not simply elongated spindle, visible in composite

w_da9f3d3374 0.3uM nuclei (blue): occasional enlarged, irregular or bi-nucleate cells vs DMSO uniform small ovals. e.g. f_1b65e7d82403 right edge cell with 2 large blue nuclei, center-top cyan nuclei larger and heterogeneous. No massive multinucleation, but clearly larger subset.
Measurement frac_large_nucleus z=+14.99 (0.03 vs 0.0) and nuc_form_factor z=-5.36 (0.893 vs 0.917) = more large/irregular nuclei, matches visible enlarged/bi-nucleate cells in composite-only view
w_da9f3d3374 0.3uM actin (red): peripheral red more intense, heterogeneous, contrasty with spiky ruffles/protrusions vs DMSO smoother cortical band. Brighter mean and patchy std.

Measurement act_mean z=+4.88 (0.486 vs 0.334), act_std z=+10.09 (0.192 vs 0.106), act_glcm_contrast z=+13.22 (0.004 vs 0.002) = higher intensity, variance and texture contrast, consistent with visible spiky heterogeneous red in composite

w_8a03ddeae8 10uM (f_a2646395beb5 3 cells, f_e1cfd248381b 2 cells): catastrophic cell loss vs DMSO, >90% empty black background. Remaining cells small, round, compact with intense bright diffuse green (tubulin) throughout, minimal spread, faint red rim only.

Measurement low cells_measured=6, cell_area z=-9.95 (2419 vs 3839), cell_major_axis z=-12.34 (65.9 vs 93.6), cell_roundness z=+39.4 (0.808 vs 0.562), cell_solidity z=+14.7 (0.944 vs 0.85), cell_eccentricity z=-32.2 (0.556 vs 0.771) = much smaller, shorter major axis, much rounder/solid/less eccentric - matches visible tiny round cells

w_8a03ddeae8 10uM tubulin (green): remaining round cells show very bright, high-contrast, heterogeneous green signal with no filamentous spread, consistent with condensed/rounded microtubule signal in apoptotic/mitotic rounding

Measurement tub_glcm_contrast z=+34.06 (0.012 vs 0.001), tub_std z=+10.06 (0.492 vs 0.147) = higher tubulin texture/heterogeneity, matches visible intense patchy green in composite; cell_nuc_area_ratio z=-15.21 (2.63 vs 4.84) consistent with cytoplasm collapse to nucleus size

notable_cells.why: large binucleate cell with 2 blue nuclei, intense green tubulin and red cortex - example of enlarged nucleus phenotype
stellate dendritic cell with multiple thin projections - example of reduced solidity/roundness

candidate_mechanisms.why: w_da9f3d3374 0.3uM shows combination of increased frac_large_nucleus, decreased nuc_form_factor, irregular stellate actin-rich morphology and increased actin intensity/contrast without classic microtubule loss - classic Aurora B failed cytokinesis > polyploid/enlarged nuclei phenotype. No DMSO-like dense clusters, but cells still attached. Fits Aurora kinase inhibitors more than pure Actin disruptors which typically round cells.

w_8a03ddeae8 10uM has only 6 cells measured, near-complete loss, tiny round bright-green cells - cytotoxicity non-specific. Insufficient morphology to assign microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer vs general protein synthesis/degradation toxicity. Composite-only view without grayscale tubulin channels limits assessment; tubulin changes likely secondary to rounding/death.

report.uncertainty: Overall compound appears dose-dependent: 0.3uM Aurora-like enlarged nuclei + actin remodeling, 10uM non-specific lethal rounding. If single MoA required: unknown due to inability to distinguish primary MoA from cytotoxicity in composite-only images; Aurora kinase inhibitor is most compatible low-dose phenotype but low confidence without DNA/tubulin grayscale and mitotic counts.

reflection.text:
This run was scored incorrect: truth mitoxantrone / DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor, annotated as DNA replication, versus my final call Protein degradation p=0.30 and earlier Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.58. Unblinding via lookup_compound e23/e24 was consistent - PubChem 4212 / ChEMBL CHEMBL58 DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor, DNA inhibitor, name and BBBC021 structure agree - and literature returned confirms this: mitoxantrone as topoisomerase II inhibitor PMID 42442624, PMID 27834128, with replication fork arrest and DNA damage signaling to DNA replication after mitoxantrone PMID 9153414, PMID 22140093. What I got right was the phenotypic strength at non-toxic doses, what I got wrong was its specificity and atlas grounding.

What the measurements actually showed: intermediate doses had strong nuclear abnormality - w_71aa1c3eef dose 5 1uM rep1 e6 frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1, nuc_solidity z=-29.8, multinucleate proxy elevated e7 z=+15.3 at 0.1uM, e2 z=+15.0 at 0.3uM - with elongated/flattened morphology cell_roundness z=-19.1 e7, -12.2 e2, cell_major_axis +14.9 and high actin texture act_glcm_contrast +26.1 e6, +13.2 e2, and reduced cell counts 72->46->45 cells vs 6 cells at 10uM e3. Dose-response over only n=4 wells, all single rep1, showed no significant dose trend for the nuclear features that motivated the call: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e9, frac_multinucleate rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e10, act_glcm_contrast rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e11, nuc_form_factor rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e14, cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e13. Only tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e12 was significant, driven largely by the 10uM well e3 tub_glcm_contrast +34.1 but with n=6 cells, cell_roundness +39.4, eccentricity -32.2 - a toxic, unreliable extreme that should have been down-weighted.

Why I was misled:

1. Non-specific morphology + microscopist anchoring. describe_phenotype e5/e15 both returned candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown with vague density higher vs lower and no DNA-replication candidate. I over-weighted enlarged/multilobed/irregular nuclei as Aurora-specific in update_hypotheses e16, putting DNA replication at 0.02 and DNA damage at 0.005 despite e6 severe solidity loss which is also expected with topoisomerase II inhibition causing segregation failure and polyploidy. The review critique was correct: multinucleation/enlarged nuclei is not Aurora-specific and occurs with microtubule/Eg5/protein-degradation mitotic failure - and with DNA replication/topoisomerase inhibitors, which my e26 literature search topoisomerase inhibitor enlarged nuclei multinucleation polyploidy phenotype returned 0 hits so I had no counter-anchor in-session.

2. Atlas contradiction ignored then over-corrected. compare_to_reference_atlas e4 NSC Protein degradation 2/2, k-neighbours Microtubule stabilizers 8/10; e8 NSC 2/4 Protein degradation, k-neighbours Protein synthesis 4/10 Microtubule destabilizers 2/10 Cholesterol-lowering 1/10; e18 NSC 2/4 Protein degradation, k-neighbours Microtubule destabilizers 5/10 Protein synthesis 4/10. At no point did NSC or k-neighbours support Aurora, and the strongest well's closest match was explicitly noted in my second rationale as vincristine 0.782 Microtubule destabilizer. My first conclusion e17 Aurora 0.58 directly contradicted e4/e8 yet I cited e2/e5/e6/e7 as key evidence. Second conclusion e22 Protein degradation 0.30 still had no Aurora support but also no DNA replication support - DNA replication remained 0.02-0.03 in all hypothesis history steps 16,20,21 with contradicting_evidence tags e18,e6.

3. Acquisition choice and budget exhaustion. I sampled only rep1 across 0.1,0.3,1,10uM after list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses 0.003-10uM. I never sampled low doses where DNA replication S-phase phenotypes are often cleanest, never acquired any replicate 2, and spent all budget before the requested validation. The review verdict request_experiment correctly identified over-calibration - all doses single replicate, 10uM n=6 - and requested acquire dose index 5 replicate 2, the strongest non-toxic phenotype, then repeat free atlas comparison/phenotype description. I attempted that as free re-analyses e18-e19 but could not acquire, and my update_hypotheses e20/e21 simply re-weighed the same 4 wells between Microtubule destabilizers 0.32/0.28 and Protein degradation 0.28/0.30 vs Aurora 0.18/0.15, still ignoring DNA replication.

In retrospect, the evidence pattern was more consistent with DNA replication stress than proteasome inhibition: reproducible large/irregular nuclei and multinucleation at 0.1-1uM with moderate cell loss, absent tubulin phenotype at non-toxic doses, and literature linking mitoxantrone to topoisomerase II-mediated cleavage and replication arrest PMID 9153414, PMID 22140093, PMID 42442624, PMID 27834128. I had the compound identity e23-e25 but did not integrate it blinded as I should have; even without unblinding, the lack of NSC support for Aurora and the non-significant dose trends e9-e11,e14 plus toxic 10uM anchor e3 should have kept p well below 0.58 and forced explicit testing of DNA replication/DNA damage hypotheses before concluding.
what_was_right: Severe nuclear phenotype at 0.1-1uM correctly captured: frac_large_nucleus +61.1 e6, +15.0 e2, multinucleate +15.3 e7, nuc_solidity -29.8 e6, consistent with mitotic segregation failure seen with mitoxantrone topoisomerase II inhibition
Cell count decline rho -0.80 e13 and loss to n=6 at 10uM e3 correctly flagged toxicity at top dose, though not used to down-weight e3

Lookup and literature e23-e25 correctly unblinded mitoxantrone as DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor PMID 42442624, PMID 27834128, with replication fork arrest PMID 9153414 and DNA replication signaling PMID 22140093
what_was_wrong: Aurora 0.58 e17 despite NSC Protein degradation 2/2 e4 and 2/4 e8/e18 and zero Aurora neighbours; Protein degradation 0.30 e22 despite truth DNA replication

Misattributed non-specific features - enlarged/irregular/multinucleate nuclei, act_glcm_contrast, tub_glcm_contrast +34.1 at n=6 e3 with rho +1.00 e12 - to Aurora/microtubule/proteasome rather than topoisomerase/DNA replication

Kept DNA replication/DNA damage at 0.02/0.005 e16 and 0.03/0.01 e21 throughout, despite e8 listing DNA replication among k-neighbour classes and no significant dose trends e9-e11,e14 to justify Aurora over DNA replication

topoisomerase II-mediated cleavage arrest of replication fork progression
mitoxantrone interaction with human DNA topoisomerase II-alpha

reflection.next_experiment: ACQUIRE dose index 5 (1.0 uM) replicate 2 as requested; if budget allows also dose index 3 (0.1 uM) replicate 2 low-dose S-phase; then repeat compare_to_reference_atlas + describe_phenotype on replicated wells before any high-dose interpretation. Add free orthogonal in-silico check: DNA content /EdU texture analysis of already acquired 0.1-1uM images.

## Reflection

This run was scored incorrect: truth mitoxantrone / DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor, annotated as DNA replication, versus my final call Protein degradation p=0.30 and earlier Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.58. Unblinding via lookup_compound e23/e24 was consistent - PubChem 4212 / ChEMBL CHEMBL58 DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor, DNA inhibitor, name and BBBC021 structure agree - and literature returned confirms this: mitoxantrone as topoisomerase II inhibitor PMID 42442624, PMID 27834128, with replication fork arrest and DNA damage signaling to DNA replication after mitoxantrone PMID 9153414, PMID 22140093. What I got right was the phenotypic strength at non-toxic doses, what I got wrong was its specificity and atlas grounding.

What the measurements actually showed: intermediate doses had strong nuclear abnormality - w_71aa1c3eef dose 5 1uM rep1 e6 frac_large_nucleus z=+61.1, nuc_solidity z=-29.8, multinucleate proxy elevated e7 z=+15.3 at 0.1uM, e2 z=+15.0 at 0.3uM - with elongated/flattened morphology cell_roundness z=-19.1 e7, -12.2 e2, cell_major_axis +14.9 and high actin texture act_glcm_contrast +26.1 e6, +13.2 e2, and reduced cell counts 72->46->45 cells vs 6 cells at 10uM e3. Dose-response over only n=4 wells, all single rep1, showed no significant dose trend for the nuclear features that motivated the call: frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e9, frac_multinucleate rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e10, act_glcm_contrast rho=-0.20 p=0.8 e11, nuc_form_factor rho=-0.40 p=0.6 e14, cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 e13. Only tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 p=0 e12 was significant, driven largely by the 10uM well e3 tub_glcm_contrast +34.1 but with n=6 cells, cell_roundness +39.4, eccentricity -32.2 - a toxic, unreliable extreme that should have been down-weighted.

Why I was misled:

1. Non-specific morphology + microscopist anchoring. describe_phenotype e5/e15 both returned candidates Aurora kinase inhibitors, unknown with vague density higher vs lower and no DNA-replication candidate. I over-weighted enlarged/multilobed/irregular nuclei as Aurora-specific in update_hypotheses e16, putting DNA replication at 0.02 and DNA damage at 0.005 despite e6 severe solidity loss which is also expected with topoisomerase II inhibition causing segregation failure and polyploidy. The review critique was correct: multinucleation/enlarged nuclei is not Aurora-specific and occurs with microtubule/Eg5/protein-degradation mitotic failure - and with DNA replication/topoisomerase inhibitors, which my e26 literature search topoisomerase inhibitor enlarged nuclei multinucleation polyploidy phenotype returned 0 hits so I had no counter-anchor in-session.

2. Atlas contradiction ignored then over-corrected. compare_to_reference_atlas e4 NSC Protein degradation 2/2, k-neighbours Microtubule stabilizers 8/10; e8 NSC 2/4 Protein degradation, k-neighbours Protein synthesis 4/10 Microtubule destabilizers 2/10 Cholesterol-lowering 1/10; e18 NSC 2/4 Protein degradation, k-neighbours Microtubule destabilizers 5/10 Protein synthesis 4/10. At no point did NSC or k-neighbours support Aurora, and the strongest well's closest match was explicitly noted in my second rationale as vincristine 0.782 Microtubule destabilizer. My first conclusion e17 Aurora 0.58 directly contradicted e4/e8 yet I cited e2/e5/e6/e7 as key evidence. Second conclusion e22 Protein degradation 0.30 still had no Aurora support but also no DNA replication support - DNA replication remained 0.02-0.03 in all hypothesis history steps 16,20,21 with contradicting_evidence tags e18,e6.

3. Acquisition choice and budget exhaustion. I sampled only rep1 across 0.1,0.3,1,10uM after list_available_experiments e1 showed 8 doses 0.003-10uM. I never sampled low doses where DNA replication S-phase phenotypes are often cleanest, never acquired any replicate 2, and spent all budget before the requested validation. The review verdict request_experiment correctly identified over-calibration - all doses single replicate, 10uM n=6 - and requested acquire dose index 5 replicate 2, the strongest non-toxic phenotype, then repeat free atlas comparison/phenotype description. I attempted that as free re-analyses e18-e19 but could not acquire, and my update_hypotheses e20/e21 simply re-weighed the same 4 wells between Microtubule destabilizers 0.32/0.28 and Protein degradation 0.28/0.30 vs Aurora 0.18/0.15, still ignoring DNA replication.

In retrospect, the evidence pattern was more consistent with DNA replication stress than proteasome inhibition: reproducible large/irregular nuclei and multinucleation at 0.1-1uM with moderate cell loss, absent tubulin phenotype at non-toxic doses, and literature linking mitoxantrone to topoisomerase II-mediated cleavage and replication arrest PMID 9153414, PMID 22140093, PMID 42442624, PMID 27834128. I had the compound identity e23-e25 but did not integrate it blinded as I should have; even without unblinding, the lack of NSC support for Aurora and the non-significant dose trends e9-e11,e14 plus toxic 10uM anchor e3 should have kept p well below 0.58 and forced explicit testing of DNA replication/DNA damage hypotheses before concluding.

What was right:
- Severe nuclear phenotype at 0.1-1uM correctly captured: frac_large_nucleus +61.1 e6, +15.0 e2, multinucleate +15.3 e7, nuc_solidity -29.8 e6, consistent with mitotic segregation failure seen with mitoxantrone topoisomerase II inhibition
- Cell count decline rho -0.80 e13 and loss to n=6 at 10uM e3 correctly flagged toxicity at top dose, though not used to down-weight e3
- Lookup and literature e23-e25 correctly unblinded mitoxantrone as DNA topoisomerase II alpha inhibitor PMID 42442624, PMID 27834128, with replication fork arrest PMID 9153414 and DNA replication signaling PMID 22140093

What was wrong or missed:
- Aurora 0.58 e17 despite NSC Protein degradation 2/2 e4 and 2/4 e8/e18 and zero Aurora neighbours; Protein degradation 0.30 e22 despite truth DNA replication
- Misattributed non-specific features - enlarged/irregular/multinucleate nuclei, act_glcm_contrast, tub_glcm_contrast +34.1 at n=6 e3 with rho +1.00 e12 - to Aurora/microtubule/proteasome rather than topoisomerase/DNA replication
- Kept DNA replication/DNA damage at 0.02/0.005 e16 and 0.03/0.01 e21 throughout, despite e8 listing DNA replication among k-neighbour classes and no significant dose trends e9-e11,e14 to justify Aurora over DNA replication

Proposed next experiment: ACQUIRE dose index 5 (1.0 uM) replicate 2 as requested; if budget allows also dose index 3 (0.1 uM) replicate 2 low-dose S-phase; then repeat compare_to_reference_atlas + describe_phenotype on replicated wells before any high-dose interpretation.
